samples.application_text: A hospital must choose how much capacity to reserve before demand is known. Underestimating demand delays care, while overestimating it leaves capacity idle. To inform this decision, we propose an estimator of the demand distribution using repeated daily measurements. We plan to evaluate the estimator’s performance in future work.

Hospitals must choose how much capacity to reserve before demand is known. Underestimating demand delays care, while overestimating it leaves capacity idle. This trade-off makes the distribution of demand a central input into capacity planning: hospitals need to assess the likelihood of demand exceeding or falling short of reserved capacity. We propose an estimator of the demand distribution using repeated daily measurements. Evaluation of the estimator is planned.

A hospital must choose how much capacity to reserve before demand is known. Reserving too little delays care, while reserving too much leaves capacity idle. This tradeoff makes the demand distribution relevant to capacity planning: it describes the likelihood that demand will exceed or fall short of a chosen capacity level. We propose an estimator of this distribution using repeated daily measurements and plan to evaluate its performance.
